# Voice corpus measurements

**Task:** F-06 · **Corpus:** `dg-pp` build `3e81bd1f069b` (clipVersion 1, created 2026-10-28T00:27:02+00:00) · **Generated by:** `scripts/measure_corpus.py`

All numbers below are produced by the committed script; nothing is hand-edited. The run is deterministic for a fixed corpus build and a fixed script revision.

## How to reproduce

Corpus cache: `${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/rasp-corpus` (registry + clips, fetched from https://dg-pp.livive.net/). Nothing is written inside the repo except this document. Once F-03 has vendored the corpus, run the same command with `--cache web` to measure the committed copy instead of the network cache.

```sh
python3 -m venv scripts/.venv
scripts/.venv/bin/pip install -r scripts/requirements.txt
scripts/.venv/bin/python scripts/measure_corpus.py
```

Coverage: **54 voices x 26 phrases = 1404 clips** (full corpus, no sampling). `--sample N` processes every Nth voice (sorted by voice id, all 26 phrases); this run used **`--sample 1`**.

### Method

- Decode: `ffmpeg -i <clip> -ac 1 -ar 48000 -f f32le` (Opus is natively 48 kHz; the source is mono).
- Levels: peak / RMS dBFS over the whole decoded clip; DC offset is the sample mean; LUFS-I is BS.1770-4 K-weighting with 400 ms blocks, 100 ms hop and absolute −70 / relative −10 LU gating.
- Clipping: samples with `|x| >= 0.999`.
- Silence: 10 ms sliding RMS envelope, threshold −45 dBFS, minimum run 20 ms. Head/tail are measured from the first/last above-threshold run, so isolated clicks below 20 ms are ignored. This is the same rule P-04 needs for trimming.
- F0: YIN over 40 ms frames, 10 ms hop, search band 60–400 Hz, absolute threshold 0.20, voiced gate 0.35, 5-frame median smoothing. Reported median / p10 / p90 are over **voiced frames across all 26 phrases** of a voice, after pooling frames (not a mean of per-clip medians).
- HNR: crude, `10*log10(r/(1-r))` from the normalised autocorrelation of the 40 ms frame at the detected lag; median over voiced frames. Compare voices, do not read it as an absolute studio figure.
- Spectral centroid: median over 25 ms Hann frames above the energy floor.

## 4. Flags

### 4.1 Clipping

No clip reaches `|x| >= 0.999`. Loudest sample in the corpus: **-0.59 dBFS** (`am_michael/fancy-a-game`). The decoder output never reaches full scale, so no headroom-driven level change is needed before DSP (true-peak/overs is not measured here).

### 4.2 DC offset

No clip exceeds `|DC| > 0.01`. Largest absolute offset in the corpus is **-0.00070** (`jm_kumo/you-got-me`), i.e. about -63.1025 dBFS of DC. No DC-blocking stage is required for correctness; a bypass-path DC blocker is optional.

### 4.3 Registry duration mismatches

**31 clips differ from `registry.durationMs` by more than 20 ms.** Largest: -27.4 ms (`bf_lily/nice-one`).

Decoded-minus-registry duration: median **-7.5 ms**, p05/p95 -8.0/-7.1 ms. The main cluster is a constant offset (Opus pre-skip / container timing). 31 clips (**2.2%**) sit an extra ~20 ms lower (max -27.4 ms), consistent with the bake rounding the frame count up by one 20 ms Opus frame. `ffprobe` agrees with the registry (it reports the 1.161 s container duration for a clip that decodes to 1.134 s), so this is container padding, not a bad registry field. D-02 should treat `durationMs` as approximate (+/- one frame) and use the decoded sample count as truth.

### 4.5 Gender label vs measured F0

Rule used: a **male**-labelled voice with median F0 >= 165 Hz, or a **female**-labelled voice with median F0 <= 145 Hz, is reported as a contradiction. These are conventional band edges, not hard truths; a falsetto male or a very low female is possible.

| voice | label | F0 med | p10 | p90 | grade |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `am_fenrir` | male | 171.4 | 93 | 198 | C+ |
| `zm_yunxi` | male | 175.0 | 128 | 211 | — |
| `am_santa` | male | 267.8 | 120 | 340 | D- |
| `zm_yunxia` | male | 315.5 | 240 | 361 | — |

Read these as *label* problems, not corpus defects: the presets are defined in pitch/formant space, so a mislabelled voice only affects cohort averaging. Do not silently reassign genders in code; record it in `voice-baselines.json` (Q-01) and leave the registry alone.

Low HNR here is consistent with 32 kbps Opus plus breathy voice models; it is a reason to avoid these voices as *pitch* anchors, not a reason to exclude them from the product (D7 already bars them from calibration where the language does not match).

## 5. Implications for the DSP implementer

### 5.1 `N` and hop (D2's 2048 @ 48 kHz)

Measured F0 across the corpus: voice medians **79–323 Hz**; pooled p10 as low as **64 Hz** and p90 as high as **373 Hz**. `N=2048` gives a bin spacing of **23.44 Hz** and a 42.7 ms window.

- Lowest p10 among clean voices (HNR >= 8 dB, voiced >= 45%): **71 Hz** = **3.0 bins** at `N=2048`. That clears the 3-bins-per-period rule of thumb (floor 70.3 Hz). The raw minimum is 64 Hz (`bm_lewis`, HNR 4.9), which is a tracker artifact on a breathy voice and should not size the FFT. `N=1024` (46.9 Hz bins, 3-bin floor 141 Hz) would fail for most female voices.
- At **−12 st** the same clean low voice lands at **36 Hz** = **1.4 bins** at `N=2048`. That matters **only for a stage that analyses the shifted output** (P-03's envelope correction), which needs **`N=4096`** there (one octave down = 3.0 bins at `N=4096`). The pitch-shift stage analyses the **input**, so `N=2048` remains correct at every ratio (DECISIONS D19); choosing the shifter's window from the output F0 was measurably worse. `N=1024` has no safe use on this corpus.
- Hop: at `H=512` (75% overlap) the unambiguous phase-deviation bound is `sr/(2H) = 46.9 Hz`, i.e. **2.0 bins** — a comfortable margin for identity phase locking when a +12 st shift moves partials by up to a bin. At `H=1024` the bound shrinks to **one bin** (23.4 Hz), which is marginal for the brightest voices (p90 373 Hz, with harmonics well above). **Keep `hop = N/4`, i.e. 512 at `N=2048`.**
- Consequence for P-01: keep the framing constant across the corpus (no adaptive `N` per clip). Choose `N` per *preset/render call*, not per voice, so A/B and golden renders stay comparable.

### 5.2 Pitch calibration anchors

English only, per D7, and both pass the quality gate (no clipping, |DC| small, HNR >= 8, no integrity failure):

| use | voice | F0 med | p10–p90 | HNR | grade | why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| low anchor | `am_onyx` | 88.4 | 71–104 | 9.2 | D | lowest clean English male; exercises +12 st and `deep` |
| high anchor | `af_aoede` | 221.3 | 160–255 | 14.3 | C+ | cleanest voice in the top of the English female range |


Use the low anchor to test that +12 st does not produce octave errors or a phase-vocoder buzz at high F0, and the high anchor to test −12 st where the shifted F0 approaches `N`'s resolution limit. For a mid reference use `af_kore` (191 Hz).

For maximum-range stress (a −12 st shift at the very top of the corpus), also render `bf_alice` (248 Hz, HNR 9.3, grade D). It is 27 Hz above the high anchor and is a *stress* case, not a calibration target, because its p10–p90 spread (14.2 st) shows tracker noise as well as intonation.

Do **not** use `zh`/`ja` voices as pitch anchors, even though several have excellent HNR. Their F0 movement carries lexical tone (D11), so a preset tuned on them would chase meaning-bearing pitch rather than voice size. Be careful with the metric here: clean `zh`/`ja` voices show a median p10–p90 of 8.2 st vs 10.0 st for clean English, i.e. **less** spread than English, because this measurement cannot separate tone from intonation and tracker noise. The reason to exclude them is D7/D11 (wrong signal to optimise), not a measured spread.

### 5.3 What P-04 must trim

Median head silence is **40 ms**, median tail **65 ms**; p90 is **55 ms / 108 ms** and the worst cases are **143 ms of head** and **524 ms of tail**. 6 clips exceed 100 ms of head silence and 170 exceed 100 ms of tail silence (0.4% and 12.1% of the corpus); 0 / 21 exceed 250 ms.

So P-04 cannot rely on a fixed pad: it needs real endpoint detection at −45 dBFS with a 20 ms minimum run, then a 5 ms fade. Budget **p90 of 55 ms head / 108 ms tail**, worst case **524 ms**; a fixed 300 ms pad would still miss the worst tail and would add ~0.6 s of dead air to most clips. Trimming must happen *before* the STFT so the phase vocoder does not smear silence into the first phoneme, and before any duration-alignment against `registry.durationMs` (which includes the silence).

**Coverage:** the 6 English picks span **148–248 Hz female** and **88–162 Hz male**. Measured English cohorts are 148–248 Hz female and 79–162 Hz male (males with a contradictory label excluded). The picks stop at 88 Hz on the male side because `bm_lewis` (79 Hz) fails the quality gate (HNR 4.9 dB, 38% voiced), not because its pitch is implausible.


**Verdict: D13's 12-voice shape stands, with 2 substitutions.**

All 12 pass the `sha256`/`bytes`, clipping and DC checks. HNR and any other measured caveat are in the table above.

**Amended:** `bm_lewis` (low, 79 Hz) was rejected (HNR 4.9 dB, 38% voiced); used `am_onyx` (88 Hz) instead. `am_santa` (high, 268 Hz) was rejected (HNR 4.4 dB, label/pitch contradiction); used `am_eric` (162 Hz) instead.

Why these 12 are enough for D13's purpose: the English six cover the pitch extremes that stress the vocoder (low male at the +12 st end, high female at the −12 st end) plus a mid voice for unbiased A/B; `zh` and `ja` are the two languages with lexical F0 (D11's hard gates), so one male and one female each test the monotone warning rather than only its happy path; `hi` and `es` give one non-tonal, non-English point each for the robot chain's language-safety pass (Q-08).

`es` is the weakest slot: all three Spanish voices are under 8 dB HNR (best `ef_dora`, 7.9 dB), so D13's single Spanish voice cannot also be a quality anchor. That is acceptable for a language-safety pass, not for pitch tuning.

Caveat: `zh`/`ja` picks are chosen for HNR and a representative (not extreme) pitch, so they are **not** pitch-range anchors — their F0 movement is lexical. Use them for language-gate and robot tests, not for natural pitch-preset tuning. `zm_yunjian` is the cleanest male-consistent Mandarin male; its HNR (6.7 dB) is a known limitation of the `zh` male cohort.

## 7. Limits of these measurements

- F0 is YIN on 32 kbps Opus; octave errors are possible on breathy frames even after median smoothing. Per-voice medians are stable to a few Hz; p10/p90 are not. Voices with HNR < 8 dB (e.g. `bm_lewis`, `am_santa`, `zm_yunyang`) show wide or octave-spaced F0 clusters: use their medians, ignore their spreads.
- HNR is autocorrelation-based, not a perceptual measure; use it for ranking, not as an absolute threshold.
- Silence thresholds are absolute dBFS, so a future re-bake that changes normalisation will change the trim numbers. Re-run this script after any registry build change.
- No formant/LPC measurements here; those belong to Q-01 (`voice-baselines.json`).
